title: Transfinite gluing of cellwise simplicial extensions
statement: Use simplicial sets, simplicial subsets and simplicial maps from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\theta$ be a small ordinal and $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$ an increasing family of simplicial subsets of a small simplicial set $X_\theta$, with $X_\beta=\bigcup_{\alpha<\beta}X_\alpha$ for every nonzero limit ordinal $\beta\leq\theta$. For each $\alpha<\theta$ let $A_\alpha\hookrightarrow B_\alpha$ be any degreewise injective simplicial map, with a map $A_\alpha\to X_\alpha$, and suppose the resulting square with bottom right corner $X_{\alpha+1}$ is a pushout, so $X_{\alpha+1}\cong X_\alpha\amalg_{A_\alpha}B_\alpha$. Let $E$ be any simplicial set and $f_0:X_0\to E$ a simplicial map. Suppose that for every $\alpha<\theta$ and every simplicial map $g:X_\alpha\to E$ whose restriction to $X_0$ is $f_0$, the composite $A_\alpha\to X_\alpha\xrightarrow{g}E$ extends to a simplicial map $B_\alpha\to E$. Then there are simplicial maps $f_\alpha:X_\alpha\to E$ for all $\alpha\leq\theta$, starting at the given $f_0$, such that $f_\beta|_{X_\alpha}=f_\alpha$ whenever $\alpha\leq\beta\leq\theta$. In particular $f_\theta$ extends $f_0$. The assertion permits $\theta=0$, empty $X_0$, and arbitrary coproducts of cell inclusions as $A_\alpha\hookrightarrow B_\alpha$.

proof.text: For each $\alpha\leq\theta$, let $F_\alpha$ be the set of simplicial maps $g:X_\alpha\to E$ whose restriction along $X_0\hookrightarrow X_\alpha$ is $f_0$. For $\alpha\leq\beta$ let $\rho_{\beta\alpha}:F_\beta\to F_\alpha$ be restriction. Identity and composition of restrictions hold, and $F_0$ has the single prescribed element $f_0$. A compatible family in these sets is therefore exactly a family of extensions as in the conclusion.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p.250: organize the successive extensions as an inverse system of maps on the stages.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha<\theta$ and $g\in F_\alpha$. By the hypothesis, the composite $A_\alpha\to X_\alpha\xrightarrow{g}E$ has an extension $h:B_\alpha\to E$. The assumed pushout square $X_{\alpha+1}\cong X_\alpha\amalg_{A_\alpha}B_\alpha$ and the equality of $h$ with $g$ on $A_\alpha$ give, by the pushout universal property, a unique simplicial map $g^+:X_{\alpha+1}\to E$ restricting to $g$ on $X_\alpha$ and to $h$ on $B_\alpha$. Since $g$ extends $f_0$, so does $g^+$; hence $g^+\in F_{\alpha+1}$ and $\rho_{\alpha+1,\alpha}(g^+)=g$. Thus every successor restriction map is surjective. This argument uses only the displayed pushout, so it also covers an arbitrary coproduct of cell inclusions presented as one degreewise-injective map.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p.250: successor-stage extension across each attached cell and gluing along its boundary.

proof.text: Let $0<\beta\leq\theta$ be a limit ordinal and let $(g_\alpha)_{\alpha<\beta}$ be a compatible family with $g_\alpha\in F_\alpha$. For a simplex $x\in (X_\beta)_n$, continuity gives some $\alpha<\beta$ with $x\in (X_\alpha)_n$; define $g_\beta(x):=g_\alpha(x)$. If another stage contains $x$, compatibility makes the value equal. Every simplicial operator sends $x$ to a simplex in the same $X_\alpha$, so these degreewise values commute with all operators and define a simplicial map $g_\beta:X_\beta\to E$. It restricts to every $g_\alpha$ and hence to $f_0$, so $g_\beta\in F_\beta$. Therefore every compatible family below a nonzero limit stage lifts to that stage.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p.250: take the degreewise union at limit stages.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-well-ordered-inverse-system-section] to the small well-ordered set $J=\{\alpha\mid \alpha\leq\theta\}$, with $F_\alpha$ and $\rho_{\beta\alpha}$ from step 1. Step 2 supplies the required surjectivity at each nonmaximal successor, and step 3 supplies the required lifting of every compatible family at each nonzero limit. Prescribing the bottom element $f_0\in F_0$, the cited result gives a compatible family $(f_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$. In particular $f_\theta$ extends $f_0$, and compatibility gives $f_\beta|_{X_\alpha}=f_\alpha$ for all $\alpha\leq\beta\leq\theta$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed p.250: transfinite recursion with fixed initial data.

proof.text: When $\theta=0$, the index set has only its bottom element and the given map $f_0$ itself is the required family. If $X_0$ is empty, the same construction starts from its unique empty map, and no step changes. The proof never uses more than the stated pushouts, successor extension hypothesis, and degreewise unions at limits, so empty stages and arbitrary coproducts of cell inclusions are included exactly as asserted.
